pages.purpose: Workout tracker. From top to bottom it shows a gamified Strength Rank 'arena', a per-day exercise logger (the 'GT' tracker) with prefill-from-last-session progression, a rest timer, coach notes, and an exercise progress chart. A legacy 'Progressive Overload Coach' (PO) app is still on the page: most of its UI is hidden, but its JS still runs and syncs, and parts of it remain visible.
pages.screensOfScrollOnPhone: About 5-7 iPhone screens for a 6-exercise day. Strength Rank alone takes about 1.5-2 screens: hero ~330px, stats ~70px, closest-rank card ~60px, then a 2-column grid with one card per exercise in the plan, unranked ones included. The tracker takes ~2.5-3 screens: each mobile exercise card is ~300px. Coach Notes is ~0.4 screen, the Progress chart ~0.3, and the legacy title/gear sits at the very bottom. The actual logging starts about 2 screens down.
pages.designNotes: Dark (#0a0a0b), but with at least three competing visual languages. (1) The rank section is styled like a game: tier-coloured neon aura, a spinning conic orbit ring, a floating hexagon emblem, 3 animated sparks, a looping sheen on the LP bar, and count-up numbers. Several of these animations loop forever. (2) Each GT exercise card gets its own emoji and colour from a keyword table (🦵 squat blue, 🍑 glute pink, 💪 curl amber...). That colour is overridden by the rank tier colour once a lift is ranked, so card colours change as rank data loads. On top of that come green/red 'Add weight/Repeat' prep buttons, amber 🔥 'to failure' chips, and red/amber F badges. (3) The legacy PO styling is monochrome, with a monospace 'SUN, OCT 18 · PUSH DAY' pill at the very top and an h1 'Progressive Overload Coach' + gear at the very BOTTOM. The hierarchy is upside down: the page title sits at the end, the rank owns the top, and the thing you came to do (log) is in the middle. The tracker header has 5 emoji/text buttons ('🕘 History', '✚ New session', '↺ Clear', '⊞ Days', '+ Exercise') that wrap to 2 rows on a phone. Lots of 9.5-11px uppercase labels at 25-40% white, so contrast is low. Every card carries meta chips, a 'Last · …' monospace line, a Fill button, set cells, a notes field and a coach chip, so cards are dense and repetitive. The desktop table and the mobile cards are both rendered into the DOM. Genuinely nice: the Fill button with its colour-coded verb, the pop/sheen confirmation when a set is complete, and the circular rest-timer pill that sits above the bottom nav.

features.name: Strength Rank hero (tier emblem, LP bar, 'X LP to Gold')
features.whatItDoes: Estimates 1RM (Epley) from every logged 'WxR' set. Divides by the latest bodyweight from the Health row (uid:health → po_coach_weights; sex comes from po_water_v1.profile). Scores each lift against strength-standard tables and averages the top 5 into a tier (Iron→Titan) with an LP progress bar. Locked ('Log my weight') until a weigh-in exists.
features.manualInputs: None directly. It depends on (a) at least one weigh-in on the Health page and (b) sets typed in the exact 'weight x reps' format. Reps-only entries never rank.
features.valueReturned: Motivation and a sense of overall strength level. Not actionable day to day, and it doesn't help you log faster.
features.dataKeys: Reads dashboard:gym:v1:template, dashboard:gym:v1:logs, Supabase uid:health (po_coach_weights, po_water_v1.profile). Writes dashboard:gym:v1:rank ({score,tier,lp,lifts}), which is synced in uid:po-coach for a 'future friends leaderboard'. Sets window.__gymExerciseTier, which recolours the tracker cards.
features.automationPotential: Already automatic. Shrink to a one-line tier chip in the header; tap it for the detail.
features.overlapsWith: Rank stats row; per-lift rank grid; XP/level system in topbar.js; Health weight tracker

features.name: Rank stats row (🔥 day streak, workouts this week, ranked lifts)
features.whatItDoes: Three tiles. The streak counts training days and breaks after 3 straight missed days. 'This week' counts dates since Sunday that have any log, and 'ranked lifts' is a count.
features.valueReturned: A weekly consistency count is mildly useful. The ranked-lifts count is trivia.
features.automationPotential: Automatic. 'X workouts this week' belongs in the Today header or on the Home tile.
features.overlapsWith: XP streaks in topbar.js; habits streaks; index.html gym tile

features.name: Closest rank-up callout ('hit 82.5 × 8 for Gold')
features.whatItDoes: Picks the lift closest to its next tier and gives a concrete weight×8 that would reach it.
features.valueReturned: A concrete, motivating target. This is the most actionable item in the rank block.
features.automationPotential: Automatic. Fold it into that exercise's card as a 'stretch goal' line instead of a separate block.
features.overlapsWith: Fill/prescription button; per-lift rank card 'Next:' targets; coach chip; Coach Notes (5 places that tell you what to lift next)

features.name: Per-lift rank grid
features.whatItDoes: A 2-column grid with one card per exercise in the plan: tier chip, est. 1RM, ×BW ratio, LP bar. Tapping a card expands its best set plus 6/8/10-rep targets for the next tier. Unranked exercises are shown greyed out with 'no weight×reps sets yet'.
features.valueReturned: Per-lift strength context. Takes a lot of space (every exercise, including greyed bodyweight and accessory lifts) for information you might look at once a month.
features.automationPotential: Move it into a 'Progress/Stats' detail view, together with the per-exercise chart.
features.overlapsWith: Exercise Progress chart; History modal best-1RM line

features.name: Day split pill ('SUN, OCT 18 · PUSH DAY') + rotation editor modal
features.whatItDoes: Legacy PO feature. It works out today's split from a rotation list plus an anchor date, and tapping it opens an editor (rename/reorder/add/delete, 'Today is →'). It does NOT select the day in the visible tracker. It only changes the hidden legacy UI's filter.
features.manualInputs: Setup once; re-anchor whenever you skip a day
features.valueReturned: In principle, 'what am I training today'. In practice it is disconnected from the tracker below, so it can say PUSH while the tracker shows Legs.
features.automationPotential: Drop the manual rotation. Auto-select today's GT day as the next day in the plan after the last one logged (from dashboard:gym:v1:logs order), so the page opens straight to the right workout.
features.overlapsWith: GT day tabs (gtDayTabs / dashboard:gym:v1:activeDay); index.html gym tile

features.name: Tracker toolbar (History, New session, Clear, Days, + Exercise)
features.whatItDoes: Five header buttons: open the History modal, start a second session of the same day this week, clear this session's sets, manage days (rename/delete/add, plus 'Reset all data'), and add an exercise.
features.manualInputs: Occasional taps. Each needs a confirm() dialog.
features.valueReturned: Plan maintenance and history access. 'New session' and 'Clear' only exist because of the week-long session model.
features.automationPotential: Collapse into a single ⋯ menu. Drop New session/Clear if sessions are simply 'today' with last time shown as ghost values.
features.overlapsWith: Legacy Settings gear (gyms/days); coach.html, which can edit the plan via AI tool calls

features.name: Today card (date, day name, week-session note, progress bar 'x/y complete · n in progress · %')
features.whatItDoes: Shows which day you're on and the share of exercises with all sets filled. If you trained this day earlier in the week, it pins that session ('📌 Showing your Mon session — it stays until the week resets (Sat night)').
features.valueReturned: Session progress. The week-pinned session is a confusing concept: numbers from Monday stay in the inputs all week.
features.automationPotential: Show 'today' only, and show the previous session as placeholders, as the per-set placeholders already do.
features.overlapsWith: index.html gym tile ('x/y logged')

features.name: Day tabs
features.whatItDoes: One tab per plan day (e.g. Push/Pull/Legs). The selected tab is remembered.
features.manualInputs: 1 tap per session when the remembered day isn't today's
features.valueReturned: Lets you pick a workout.
features.automationPotential: Auto-select the next day in the cycle from log history. Keep the tabs as a small override.
features.overlapsWith: Legacy split pill

features.name: Exercise cards: per-set text inputs (core logging)
features.whatItDoes: Each exercise card has N set cells, each a free-text field parsed by regex ('80x8', '80kg x 8', '10', '8/right 7/left'). Unilateral lifts get separate R and L fields per set. Placeholders show last session's raw text. The value saves on every keystroke, and a complete 'WxR' value triggers a pop animation, auto-advance and the rest timer.
features.manualInputs: Every set of every exercise, every session (typically 15-28 cells per workout). One set, typed from scratch: tap the cell and type '80x8'. But the fields use inputmode="decimal", and the iOS decimal keypad very likely has no 'x' key (check on the iPhone). A fresh weight×reps can then only be entered by first tapping Fill and editing digits. Typing just '8' saves reps with no weight, which drops out of rank, volume, History PRs and the prescription weight. Full path for one set: Fitness tab (1) → scroll ~2 screens past Rank → maybe tap the day tab (1) → scroll to the card → Fill (1) → if reps differed, tap cell (1) + backspace (1) + digit (1). Roughly 4-7 taps and 3-5 swipes for the first set; later sets ~3 taps each.
features.valueReturned: This is where all the data comes from: rank, History, prescriptions, Health's body-composition estimate, the coach.html context, and the Home tile.
features.dataKeys: dashboard:gym:v1:logs → {'YYYY-MM-DD': {exId: {set0:'80x8', set0R:'…', set0F:true, notes:'…', nm:'Bench', dn:'Push'}, __new:{dayId:1}}}
features.automationPotential: Pre-fill every set with the prescription as ghost values. One tap ✓ accepts a set as planned. A −/+ reps stepper (and weight stepper) covers deviations. The hidden legacy PO UI already had a weight ± stepper and rep pills that could be reused. No free-text parsing, no keyboard.
features.overlapsWith: Hidden legacy 'Log today's top set' form

features.name: 'Last · …' line + one-tap Fill (progression prescription)
features.whatItDoes: Shows the previous session's sets and a colour-coded button. Green 'Add weight 82.5kg × 6' if avg reps ≥ repMax, 'Beat reps 80kg × 9' if in range, red 'Repeat' if below, 'Start' if no history. Tapping fills every empty set with that value, and Undo is available.
features.valueReturned: Exactly the 'tell me what to do and save me typing' value the owner wants. The best feature on the page.
features.dataKeys: derived from dashboard:gym:v1:logs + template (repMin, repMax, step, target)
features.automationPotential: Make it the default state: sets arrive already filled with the plan, so the user only confirms or adjusts.
features.overlapsWith: Coach chip; Coach Notes; rank targets; legacy Rx 'Next session'

features.name: To-failure (AMRAP) F badges + '🔥 n to failure' chips
features.whatItDoes: For exercises set up with failSets>0, the last N set cells get a dashed F badge you tap when you hit failure. History shows these sets with ⚡.
features.manualInputs: Configure failSets per exercise once; 1 tap per failure set
features.valueReturned: A marker in History. It isn't used in any recommendation logic.
features.dataKeys: exercise.failSets in template; set{i}F:true in logs (also read by coach.html as toFailureSets)
features.automationPotential: none needed

features.name: Per-exercise session notes field
features.whatItDoes: A 'Notes…' text input on every card, saved with the session.
features.valueReturned: Rarely needed. Costs ~45px on every card.
features.automationPotential: Hide behind the card's ⋯ menu.

features.name: Coach chip per card (↑ add weight / ✓ hold / ↓ reduce / log more)
features.whatItDoes: Averages reps across the last 10 log DATES (all exercises' dates, not per-exercise sessions) and labels the exercise. Updates live while typing.
features.valueReturned: Duplicates the Fill verb with a different algorithm, so the two can disagree (e.g. chip '↑ add weight' while Fill says 'Beat reps').
features.automationPotential: Remove. The single prescription covers it.
features.overlapsWith: Fill button; Coach Notes

features.name: Card ⋯ menu (Edit exercise, Move up/down, Remove)
features.whatItDoes: Per-card overflow menu for plan maintenance.
features.valueReturned: Plan editing in context
features.overlapsWith: Desktop table ↑/↓ buttons; Manage Days modal

features.name: Rest timer floating pill
features.whatItDoes: Starts automatically (90s) when a set cell becomes a complete 'WxR'. Shows a ring countdown with −15/+15/Skip, based on wall-clock time, and floats above the bottom nav. Mobile cards only.
features.valueReturned: Saves using a separate timer app. Zero effort.
features.automationPotential: Trigger it from the ✓-set confirm in a redesign. No vibration or notification at 0 yet.

features.name: Coach Notes section
features.whatItDoes: Before logging, shows a hard-coded 'Focus:' sentence per day name (push/pull/legs/upper). After logging, shows one compact row per exercise (Add/Hold/Reduce weight · reps · in/below range), refreshed with a 600ms debounce.
features.valueReturned: A third restatement of the same progression signal, plus generic text.
features.overlapsWith: Fill verb; coach chip; coach.html AI coach

features.name: Exercise Progress chart (dropdown + canvas line)
features.whatItDoes: Pick an exercise and see a line of max weight per day over the last 20 days. BUG: it reads the LEGACY store (po_coach_v1.exercises/logs), whose logging UI is hidden. Workouts logged in the current tracker (dashboard:gym:v1:logs) never appear here, so the dropdown is empty or frozen at old data.
features.valueReturned: Should be the key 'am I getting stronger' view. Right now it shows nothing new.
features.automationPotential: Rebuild from dashboard:gym:v1:logs: a small est-1RM sparkline inside each exercise card or the rank detail, with no dropdown.
features.overlapsWith: Rank grid; History modal; legacy hidden sparkline

features.name: Legacy 'Progressive Overload Coach' header + Settings gear modal
features.whatItDoes: Visible h1 plus gear at the bottom of the page. The modal edits units (kg/lb), Gyms (Home/Commercial), Days, and Export/Import/Reset JSON, all on the legacy po_coach_v1 store. Units don't affect the visible tracker, which infers kg/lb from the target text. Export omits all current GT data.
features.valueReturned: Nothing for the current tracker. The export is misleading as a 'backup'.
features.dataKeys: po_coach_v1 (units, gyms, days, exercises, logs, filterGym, filterDay, currentEx, splitRotation, splitAnchor)
features.automationPotential: Delete. Before removing the key, check whether po_coach_v1.logs holds real historic data worth migrating into the GT log format.

features.name: Hidden legacy PO card (Log top set, Next session Rx, 1RM/Best/Sessions stats, 10-session sparkline, History, Today's workout + 'Mark workout done', Past workouts)
features.whatItDoes: display:none since the GT tracker replaced it, but still rendered on every load, re-rendered on sync, and synced. 'Mark workout done' writes po_coach_workout_done.
features.valueReturned: None, apart from code weight (~1,300 lines of JS/CSS). Its weight ± stepper plus rep-pill picker is a better input pattern than the current free-text cells and is worth reusing.
features.overlapsWith: Everything in the GT tracker

features.name: Workout History modal
features.whatItDoes: Every session by date, filterable by exercise. Shows per-day set count, kg volume, the best set with est-1RM, and set chips you can edit inline (tap). You can delete a whole session or one exercise from it.
features.valueReturned: Review and fixes. A totals line (sessions, sets, total volume).
features.dataKeys: dashboard:gym:v1:logs (uses nm/dn stamps so renamed or deleted exercises still read correctly)
features.overlapsWith: Legacy Past workouts; Exercise Progress chart

features.name: Add / Edit Exercise modals
features.whatItDoes: Name, sets, rep min/max, target weight as FREE TEXT ('55 kg'; unit inferred from 'lb' in the string), step kg, to-failure count, bodyweight checkbox, unilateral checkbox, notes, delete.
features.manualInputs: About 9 fields per new exercise. Setup only.
features.valueReturned: Defines the plan the prescriptions run on.
features.automationPotential: Only name, sets and rep range are needed. Derive target and step from the first logged set. coach.html can already add or edit exercises via chat.

features.name: Manage Days modal (+ 'Reset all data')
features.whatItDoes: Rename, delete or add plan days. A destructive 'Reset all data' wipes template + logs + activeDay.
features.valueReturned: Plan structure

features.name: Cloud sync + live auto-reload
features.whatItDoes: Overrides Storage.prototype so the 6 gym keys live in memory (_dbG) and sync to Supabase row <uid>:po-coach, not to real localStorage. Pushes are merged, and logs are unioned by date and exercise. Two separate 5-second polling intervals plus visibilitychange. When another device pushes, the page force-reloads (skipped only while an input is focused). The rank engine also re-renders every 30s.
features.valueReturned: Phone↔PC consistency. The side effects are surprise page reloads mid-session, battery and data use, and other pages that read these keys from real localStorage (index.html) can see stale data.
features.dataKeys: Supabase app_state key '<uid>:po-coach' with po_coach_v1, po_coach_workout_done, dashboard:gym:v1:template, dashboard:gym:v1:logs, dashboard:gym:v1:activeDay, dashboard:gym:v1:rank, _pushAt. Consumers: coach.html (reads plan+logs, AI edits template), health.html (composition estimate from logs), index.html (gym tile + 'Log today's X workout' nudge), summary.html.
features.automationPotential: Keep the merge logic. Replace the reload-on-change with an in-place re-render, and use one poller, not three.

pages.purpose: Food diary and macro tracker. It shows a daily kcal ring with P/C/F bars against computed targets, one-tap quick-log chips, 8 micronutrient tiles, a 5-group diary, an add-food sheet with 6 tabs (Library+USDA search, Meals, Quick add, Recipe, Barcode, AI), a Weekly Verdict that adjusts calories from real weight change, and a 7-day kcal bar strip.
pages.screensOfScrollOnPhone: About 2.5-3 screens: date ~60px, hero stacked on a phone ~420px (172px ring plus macros plus 2 buttons), quick chips ~80px, micros 2 rows ~110px, 5 diary groups ~600px+ (empty groups still show 'Nothing yet'), verdict ~150px, week ~90px, footnote ~60px. The add sheet is a bottom modal and doesn't scroll the page.
pages.designNotes: More coherent than gym: one accent colour throughout. Accent aura behind the page, a gradient ring with a glow, protein/carbs/fat in pink/blue/amber, and bottom-sheet modals. A good base to build on. Busy parts: all three macro bars run an infinite sheen animation, and there's an entrance stagger on every load. The ring is 172px on phones, so the hero alone is over half a screen. Micronutrient tiles sit 4 across at 375px (~80px each, 10px text) and are mostly empty or zero, because most logged foods only have macros. They read as failure, not information. The add sheet crams 6 equal-width tabs into one row (~52px each; 'Quick add' squeezed). The diary always renders 5 group cards, empty ones included, so the page looks like a form to fill rather than a summary. The week bars have no values or target line. Emoji are used as icons (🌅☀️🌙🍎💊🎯⧉). Genuinely nice: the horizontally scrolling '⚡ Quick log' chips and the Weekly Verdict card's plain-language advice.

features.name: Date navigation (‹ Today ›)
features.whatItDoes: Step back through past days. Can't go into the future.
features.valueReturned: Backfill or review a day

features.name: Setup banner
features.whatItDoes: Shows 'No bodyweight yet → Health' or 'add height & age in Targets' until targets can be computed.
features.valueReturned: Onboarding guidance
features.dataKeys: reads BW from uid:health, profile from uid:food

features.name: Energy hero: kcal ring + Protein/Carbs/Fat bars
features.whatItDoes: Ring shows today's kcal against the target ('X left'), turning amber when over 105%. Three macro bars show eaten vs target in grams.
features.valueReturned: The answer the owner needs at a glance: how much is left today, especially protein.
features.automationPotential: Could surface on the Home page as a single line: '1,240 kcal · 95 g protein left'. health.html already has a mini food ring reading the same row.
features.overlapsWith: health.html food summary ring (fsKcal/fsRing); index.html Meals tile (which still reads the OLD Meal Prep keys)

features.name: Targets modal (Mifflin-St Jeor)
features.whatItDoes: Height, age, sex, activity, goal rate (gain/lose kg per week), protein g/kg → kcal and macro targets. Bodyweight comes automatically from Health weigh-ins. Live preview.
features.manualInputs: 6 fields, once (age and sex are seeded from Health profile if present)
features.valueReturned: Personal targets, which make the ring meaningful
features.dataKeys: uid:food → profile {heightCm, age, sex, activity, goalRate, proteinPerKg, _at}; custom {kcal, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, _at} (manual override, cleared on save)
features.automationPotential: Read height, age and sex from a single shared profile (Health/onboarding) so the user never sees this.
features.overlapsWith: Health page profile (po_water_v1.profile); onboarding.html

features.name: Copy yesterday
features.whatItDoes: Duplicates all of the previous day's entries into the viewed day, after a confirm.
features.valueReturned: Big time-saver for someone who eats similarly every day
features.automationPotential: Offer per-meal ('same breakfast as yesterday?') rather than the whole day.

features.name: ⚡ Quick log chips
features.whatItDoes: Up to 3 saved meals plus the 6 most-logged foods from the last 14 days. One tap logs the food into a meal group picked from the time of day (<11 breakfast, <16 lunch, <21 dinner, else snacks), at the default portion (1 serving or 100 g).
features.valueReturned: The 'open app, tap what you ate, done' flow. The lowest-friction logging path on either page.
features.dataKeys: derived from uid:food days + library + meals
features.automationPotential: Make this the main UI. Rank chips by time of day and day of week, and remember each food's usual portion instead of 100 g.
features.overlapsWith: Library tab; Meals tab

features.name: Micronutrient tiles (8 by default: fiber, sodium, potassium, calcium, iron, magnesium, Vit D, Vit C)
features.whatItDoes: Daily totals against RDA-style targets, green when met and red when sodium is over.
features.manualInputs: none (but only populated by USDA, barcode or recipe foods)
features.valueReturned: Little. AI estimates, quick-add, meal-prep migrations and most barcode items carry macros only, so the tiles mostly sit at 0 / target. The page's own footnote admits 'an empty micro doesn't mean zero'. Takes 2 rows of prime space.
features.dataKeys: uid:food settings.highlighted (no UI to edit it on this page); NUTR registry keys on entries[].n
features.automationPotential: At most, a weekly 'fiber low this week' insight inside the verdict.

features.name: Diary (Breakfast / Lunch / Dinner / Snacks / Supplements groups)
features.whatItDoes: Entries listed per group with protein and kcal. Each group header has a + that opens the add sheet for that group. Tap an entry to edit it.
features.manualInputs: Choose a group via its + (1 tap) before every add
features.valueReturned: A record of what you ate today
features.dataKeys: uid:food days['YYYY-MM-DD'].entries[] = {id, group, foodId, name, qty, unit, n:{kcal,protein_g,…}, src, at, updatedAt}
features.automationPotential: One global '+' with auto-grouping by time, as the quick chips already do. Collapse empty groups.
features.overlapsWith: Health page Meal Prep (dashboard:mealPrep:v1:template/daily), which is still live and still drives the Home Meals tile and 'Eat X' nudge

features.name: Supplements note
features.whatItDoes: In the Supplements group, shows 'n/m taken today — tracked on Health' from the Health stack.
features.valueReturned: A cross-link only
features.overlapsWith: Health supplement stack

features.name: Add sheet: Library tab + USDA database search
features.whatItDoes: Search your saved foods, with recent ones first. Typing 2+ characters also queries /api/food (USDA) after a 450ms debounce. Tapping a result logs it immediately at a FIXED default (100 g for per-100g foods, 1 serving otherwise) and adds USDA picks to the library.
features.manualInputs: Typical new food: Food tab (1) → group + (1) → type a search term → tap result (1). That logs 100 g. To fix the portion: tap the entry (1) → retype Amount → Save (1). About 5-6 taps plus 2 typed fields per item. A day of ~10-12 items comes to 50-70 interactions.
features.valueReturned: Accurate macros and micros for real foods
features.dataKeys: uid:food library[] = {id, name, kind:'per100'|'serving', per, unit, nutrients{…full USDA vector}, src:'usda'|'barcode'|'ai'|'custom'|'recipe'|'mealprep', ref, recipe?, updatedAt}
features.automationPotential: Ask for the portion inline (chips: 50/100/150 g or ½/1/2 servings) before logging. Remember the last portion per food. Deduplicate USDA picks by fdcId: picking the same food twice currently creates duplicate library items.
features.overlapsWith: Quick log chips; AI tab

features.name: Meals tab (saved meals)
features.whatItDoes: Logs every item of a saved meal at once. Meals ONLY come from a one-time migration of the Health page's Meal Prep templates. There is no way to create or save a meal on this page.
features.valueReturned: Fast for repeated meals, but frozen at whatever was migrated
features.dataKeys: uid:food meals[] = {id, name, items:[{foodId, qty}], updatedAt}; migrated flag; reads uid:health dashboard:mealPrep:v1:template once
features.automationPotential: Add 'save this group as a meal' from the diary, and auto-suggest meals from repeated same-time combinations.
features.overlapsWith: Health Meal Prep; Quick log chips (first 3 meals)

features.name: Quick add tab (manual macros)
features.whatItDoes: Name, amount, unit (serving/g), kcal, P, C, F, plus 12 optional micronutrient fields. Saved to the library by default.
features.manualInputs: Up to 7 fields (19 with micros) per new food
features.valueReturned: Covers foods with no database match
features.automationPotential: The AI tab makes this mostly redundant. Keep it as a fallback link.

features.name: Recipe builder tab
features.whatItDoes: Name a recipe, pick ingredients from the library with grams each, enter the cooked weight (auto-filled with the raw sum) and servings. Saves a per-100g food and logs 1 serving.
features.manualInputs: Name + N ingredient searches + N gram fields + cooked weight + servings. About 10-20 interactions, done once per recipe.
features.valueReturned: Accurate home-cooked macros for a meal-prepper. Niche.
features.dataKeys: library item with recipe {ingredients:[{foodId,g}], cookedWeightG, servings}
features.automationPotential: AI tab: 'chicken 500g, rice 300g dry, oil 1 tbsp, makes 4 boxes'.

features.name: Barcode tab
features.whatItDoes: Type a barcode, or scan with the camera where BarcodeDetector exists, and look it up via /api/barcode (Open Food Facts). Logs 100 g.
features.manualInputs: On the owner's iPhone, Safari has no BarcodeDetector, so the camera button is hidden. They must TYPE the 8-13 digits, then Look up, tap the result, and fix the 100 g portion.
features.valueReturned: Packaged-food macros, but typing 13 digits is slower than searching by name
features.automationPotential: Use a JS decoder from the allowed CDNs (e.g. ZXing) so the iPhone camera actually scans. Otherwise hide the tab on iOS.

features.name: AI estimate tab
features.whatItDoes: Type a sentence ('3 eggs, toast with butter, a banana') and POST it to /api/food (LLM, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Returns items with kcal and macros. Tap + per item to log it as 1 serving.
features.manualInputs: + (1) → AI tab (1) → type a sentence → Estimate (1) → + per item (N). About 4 + N taps and one sentence per meal.
features.valueReturned: The fastest way to log a whole new meal with its quantities. Matches the 'save time' goal.
features.dataKeys: Every AI item is pushed into library as a new 'serving' food (src:'ai'), so the library fills with one-off duplicates.
features.automationPotential: Promote it to a single text box at the top of the page ('What did you eat?') with 'Add all' in one tap. Don't save AI items to the library unless they are re-used.
features.overlapsWith: Quick add; Recipe; coach.html chat

features.name: Entry edit modal
features.whatItDoes: Change the amount (nutrients rescale), move the entry to another group, or delete it.
features.manualInputs: Tap entry → edit → Save. This is required after most library, USDA or barcode adds because of the 100 g default.
features.valueReturned: Portion correction and cleanup
features.automationPotential: Mostly unnecessary if the portion is chosen at add time.

features.name: Weekly Verdict (adaptive calories)
features.whatItDoes: Needs ≥4 logged days in the last 7 and ≥2 Health weigh-ins in the last 10 days. Compares average intake against the real weight trend (7700 kcal/kg) to infer true maintenance. Says hold, raise or ease off by ±X kcal, and has an 'Apply to targets' button. Copy bug: it always says 'You're gaining … kg/week', even for a loss goal or negative change.
features.manualInputs: Indirect: 4+ days of food logging plus 2+ weigh-ins. 1 tap to apply.
features.valueReturned: Real, self-correcting advice. The kind of 'give me info' output the owner wants.
features.dataKeys: reads uid:food days + profile.goalRate; uid:health po_coach_weights; writes custom.kcal on apply
features.automationPotential: Already automatic. Surface it on the Home page weekly. Lower the logging requirement by accepting 'typical day' estimates.

features.name: This Week bars
features.whatItDoes: 7 kcal bars for the last 7 days, scaled to target, with today/viewed day highlighted. No numbers and no target line.
features.valueReturned: Shows consistency at a glance, though it's hard to read without values
features.automationPotential: Merge into the Verdict card as a sparkline with a target line.
features.overlapsWith: Weekly Verdict; trends.html

features.name: Food library (implicit) + sync
features.whatItDoes: Every USDA, barcode, AI, quick-add or recipe pick becomes a library food. There is NO UI to rename, edit or delete library foods. Days are pruned to 400. Syncs one Supabase row, merging entries by id, pulling every 15s and on focus.
features.valueReturned: Re-use of foods. Over time the library fills with duplicates, so search results get noisier.
features.dataKeys: Supabase app_state '<uid>:food' = {library[], meals[], days{}, profile{}, custom{}, settings{highlighted}, migrated, _pushAt}; localStorage mirror 'dashboard:sync:food:v1'; XP via window.dashAddXpDaily (dashboard:xp:v1). Read by health.html foodRing().
features.automationPotential: Dedupe by name/ref automatically, and hide foods that haven't been used in 60 days.

crossCuttingObservations:
1. GYM HAS TWO APPS IN ONE FILE. The legacy 'Progressive Overload Coach' (po_coach_v1 + po_coach_workout_done) is still loaded. Its main card is display:none, but it still renders, re-renders on every sync and gets synced. Four parts of it are still visible and confusing: (a) the 'SUN · PUSH DAY' rotation pill at the top, which doesn't drive the tracker; (b) the 'Exercise Progress' chart, which ONLY reads legacy logs, so new workouts never show up in it; (c) the 'Progressive Overload Coach' title, sitting at the BOTTOM of the page; (d) a Settings gear whose units, gyms, days and Export/Import/Reset act on the dead store. Its Export doesn't include the real gym data. Removing the legacy app cuts roughly 40% of gym.html. Before deleting the po_coach_v1 key, check whether its logs hold history worth converting into the dashboard:gym:v1:logs shape.

2. 'WHAT SHOULD I LIFT' IS ANSWERED IN 5 PLACES WITH 4 ALGORITHMS: the Fill button (last session's average reps), the coach chip (average over the last 10 log dates across all exercises), the Coach Notes list (today's analysis plus generic 'Focus:' text), the rank cards' 'Next tier at X×6/8/10', and 'Closest rank-up'. They can disagree. Keep one: the Fill prescription, shown as the pre-filled value.

3. THE CORE INPUT IS THE BIGGEST FRICTION. Sets are free-text strings parsed by regex ('80x8'), entered through inputmode=decimal. On iPhone that keypad very likely has no 'x' (check on device). So a fresh weight×reps set probably can't be typed without first tapping Fill. A bare '8' saves reps with no weight, and those sets quietly drop out of rank, volume, PRs and prescriptions. Reaching the logger also means scrolling past ~2 screens of Strength Rank. A full session is 15-28 set cells. Suggested redesign: open on today's workout (day picked automatically), every set pre-filled from the prescription, one ✓ per set, and ± steppers for misses. The hidden legacy UI already has a weight ± stepper and rep-pill picker that can be reused. Result: about 1 tap per set and no keyboard.

4. FOOD ALREADY HAS LOW-FRICTION PATHS BUT HIDES THEM: quick-log chips (1 tap, auto meal group), AI sentence parsing, and Copy yesterday. Meanwhile the page leads with a 172px ring, 8 mostly-empty micronutrient tiles, 5 empty diary groups and a 6-tab add sheet. Every library, USDA or barcode pick logs a fixed 100 g / 1 serving and has to be edited afterwards (+3 taps per item). There's no library management, so duplicates pile up, and AI items are always saved to the library. iPhone Safari can't scan barcodes (no BarcodeDetector), so that tab means typing 13 digits. Meals can't be created on this page; they only came from a one-time Health Meal Prep import.

5. DUPLICATE OR OVERLAPPING SYSTEMS ACROSS PAGES: Health still has the full Meal Prep feature (dashboard:mealPrep:v1:template/daily/settings/coach), and index.html's Meals tile and 'Eat X' nudge still read Meal Prep, not the Food row. Health has its own food ring that reads uid:food. Bodyweight lives in uid:health → po_coach_weights, and both gym rank and food targets/verdict depend on it. The supplements stack lives on Health and is echoed in Food. Streaks exist in gym rank, the topbar XP system and habits. coach.html reads the gym plan and logs and can edit the gym template through AI tool calls, which is a real automation hook to keep.

6. INSIGHTS THAT ARE ACTUALLY WORTH KEEPING (automatic, actionable): the gym prescription (next weight × reps per exercise), the rest timer, food kcal/protein left today, and the Food Weekly Verdict (true maintenance plus a ±kcal recommendation with one-tap apply). All four could sit on one Home 'Today' card, for example 'Push · Bench 82.5×8 first · 1,240 kcal / 95 g protein left · verdict: hold'. Then the deep pages are only opened to log.

7. VISUAL NOISE VS 'EYE-PULLING': gym mixes a neon game-tier aesthetic (spinning orbit, floating emblem, sparks, looping sheen), per-exercise emoji and colours that change once the rank data loads, green/red/amber status colours, and leftover monochrome legacy styling. Food runs 3 infinite sheen animations on the macro bars. There's a lot of 9.5-11px, 25-40%-white text, and emoji stand in for icons everywhere. One focal visual per page (gym: today's workout; food: the remaining-today ring) with a single accent would look more intentional and less like a chore list.

8. SYNC SIDE-EFFECTS THAT HURT THE EXPERIENCE: gym polls Supabase from 2 separate 5-second intervals and calls location.reload() whenever another device pushes (skipped only while an input is focused), so the page can reload mid-workout. Rank also re-renders every 30s, and food polls every 15s. Gym keys are kept in memory by overriding Storage.prototype, not written to real localStorage. Other pages that read localStorage directly (index.html reads dashboard:gym:v1:*) may see stale data unless they sync themselves.

9. DATA KEYS TO PRESERVE IN ANY REDESIGN. Supabase row '<uid>:po-coach' holds dashboard:gym:v1:template ([{id, name, exercises:[{id, name, sets, repMin, repMax, target, step, failSets, bw, unilateral, notes}]}]), dashboard:gym:v1:logs ({date:{exId:{setN, setNR, setNF, notes, nm, dn}, __new}}), dashboard:gym:v1:activeDay, dashboard:gym:v1:rank, plus legacy po_coach_v1 and po_coach_workout_done. Supabase row '<uid>:food' holds {library, meals, days, profile, custom, settings, migrated}, mirrored to localStorage as 'dashboard:sync:food:v1'. Both pages read '<uid>:health' (po_coach_weights, po_water_v1.profile, stack:items, stack:taken:<date>, dashboard:mealPrep:v1:template). XP goes through window.dashAddXpDaily (dashboard:xp:v1 → uid:xp). APIs used: /api/food (GET USDA search, POST AI parse), /api/barcode.
